issue: The lesson's summary table gives 'completed-contract policy change under a new standard's transition' as an example of a change in accounting principle, with the treatment 'Retrospective'. The lesson never states the governing rule: a change required by a new ASU follows that ASU's own transition provisions (ASC 250-10-45-3), and full retrospective application is only the default when the ASU has none. Learners will conclude that adopting a new standard is always fully retrospective. Completed-contract is also a pre-ASC 606 (ASC 605-35) method, which makes the example confusing as well as dated.
evidence: Table row 1, column 'Example': 'FIFO → weighted average; completed-contract policy change under a new standard's transition'; Treatment: 'Retrospective'. Recent standards the exam tests used other transitions: ASC 606 allowed modified retrospective (cumulative effect to opening RE in the year of adoption), ASC 842 an optional transition method, CECL (ASC 326) modified retrospective, and ASU 2023-08 crypto assets a cumulative-effect adjustment. Nothing in the lesson body, takeaways or flowchart mentions transition provisions. ASC 250-10-45-2 and 45-3 are missing.
source: ASC 250-10-45-2, 250-10-45-3 (report a change required by a new Codification update per its transition provisions); ASC 250-10-45-5 (retrospective application when the update has no transition provisions)
fix: Replace the second example with an unambiguous voluntary change (e.g., 'LIFO → FIFO'). Add a bullet under 'Retrospective application': 'A change required by a new ASU follows that ASU's transition provisions (often modified retrospective, with a cumulative-effect adjustment to opening RE of the adoption year). Retrospective application is the default only for voluntary (preferable) changes and for ASUs with no transition guidance (ASC 250-10-45-3).' Add a matching key takeaway and one practice MCQ.

issue: Lesson–item alignment gaps: practice items test three rules that the lesson never teaches. (1) The impracticability fallback: the lesson says 'unless impracticable' four times but never says what happens then. far-chg-08, -14 and -28 test 'apply prospectively from the earliest date practicable' (and the LIFO base layer). (2) The exclusions from a change in reporting entity (a business combination, or consolidating a VIE, is not one): tested by far-chg-04(b) and relevant to far-chg-26. (3) Correcting entries when the current year's books are still open (debit or credit RE against the current-year expense): tested by far-chg-18.
evidence: The lesson body has 'Retrospective application' (3 steps) and 'Error corrections' sections only. The only impracticability content is the takeaway 'Changes to LIFO are usually prospective because retrospective application is impracticable.' The lesson defines reporting-entity changes only by the example 'consolidated instead of individual statements'. No worked or faded example shows a correction with the current year open.
source: ASC 250-10-45-6, 45-7 (impracticability; prospective from the earliest date practicable); ASC 250-10-20 'Change in the reporting entity' (business combinations and VIE consolidation excluded)
fix: Add to 'Retrospective application': 'If the period-specific effects are impracticable, apply to the earliest period practicable and adjust that period's opening balances. If even the cumulative effect is impracticable (typical for a change to LIFO), apply prospectively from the earliest date practicable; beginning inventory becomes the base layer (ASC 250-10-45-6, 45-7).' Add a 'Change in reporting entity' line listing the three ASC 250-10-20 cases and the business-combination/VIE exclusion. Add a short example: Year 1 accrual omitted, found in Year 2 before closing → Dr RE, Cr current-year expense.

issue: The stem describes beginning to consolidate a former equity-method investee, which in practice means obtaining control: a business combination achieved in stages (ASC 805), accounted for prospectively. ASC 250-10-20 says that is NOT a change in reporting entity. The stem forces the key by appending 'because of a change in the reporting entity'. That phrase (i) gives the classification away, leaving pure recall, and (ii) teaches that moving from the equity method to consolidation is a reporting-entity change, the misconception the exam tests. Under the natural reading, distractor (a) 'Prospectively, from the change date' is the correct treatment. The key also says 'for all periods' where the rule is 'all periods presented'.
evidence: ASC 250-10-20: a change in reporting entity is limited mainly to (a) consolidated or combined statements in place of individual entities' statements, (b) changing the specific subsidiaries in the consolidated group, (c) changing the entities in combined statements. 'Neither a business combination accounted for by the acquisition method nor the consolidation of a VIE … is a change in reporting entity.' A step acquisition remeasures the previously held equity interest at fair value through earnings and consolidates from the acquisition date (ASC 805-10-25-10). far-chg-04(b) in this same module says so correctly ('A business combination isn't a change in reporting entity').
fix: Rewrite the stem as an unambiguous reporting-entity change without naming the category, e.g.: 'A parent that has always issued parent-only financial statements begins issuing consolidated statements that include its long-held subsidiaries. How is the change reported?' Key: 'Retrospectively, recasting all periods presented'. Add to the explanation: 'Obtaining control of an investee (business combination) is not a change in reporting entity; it is accounted for prospectively under ASC 805.'

issue: Pure-recall items are labeled skill 'analysis', two levels too high, which inflates the module's analysis share used for Blueprint skill-mix targets. far-chg-28 asks for the impracticability rule with no facts. Its twin far-chg-14 is labeled 'application'. far-chg-16 and -27 ask how a cash-to-GAAP switch is classified, the same rule-recall as flashcard fc5. far-chg-04 and -01, which classify changes the same way, are labeled 'remembering'. far-chg-26 states the classification in the stem and asks only for its treatment.
evidence: Labels in items.json: far-chg-16 analysis/3, far-chg-26 analysis/3, far-chg-27 analysis/3, far-chg-28 analysis/3. Blueprint FAR-III.A R&U task: 'Identify changes in accounting principle, … estimate, … reporting entity and error corrections and their required treatment'. Analysis means examining interrelationships, detecting errors and investigating; none of these items requires it. Module practice and exam labels are R 4 / App 13 / Ana 14 (45%, the top of FAR's 35–45% band); relabeled honestly, analysis drops to about 5 items.
source: AICPA 2026 FAR Blueprint skill definitions; review/reference/blueprint-tasks.csv FAR-III.A.1
fix: Relabel far-chg-16, -26, -27 and -28 as skill 'remembering' (difficulty: see the separate difficulty finding). If analysis-level coverage is wanted, replace one of the duplicates (far-chg-27 or -28) with a genuine analysis item, e.g. a prepared restatement schedule with two errors to detect and correct.

issue: Skill labels are one level off, almost all inflated. Single-step computations and rule applications are labeled 'analysis'. Structurally identical items are labeled inconsistently: far-chg-24 (useful-life revision, analysis, difficulty 3) vs. far-x3-13 (the same computation, application, difficulty 2). The TBS far-tbs-r3-changes-errors is labeled 'analysis' but has the same classify, compute and record-JE structure as far-tbs-u12-changes, labeled 'application'. far-chg-14 (impracticability rule with no facts) is labeled 'application' but is recall.
evidence: far-chg-19: 36,000 ÷ 3 = 12,000. far-chg-21: 20,000 × 0.75 = 15,000 (the same calc as far-chg-02, labeled application). far-chg-22: 80,000 × 8/36. far-chg-24: 36,000 ÷ 3. far-chg-10: the indirect-effects rule applied to a stated scenario. far-chg-chk1: classify a non-GAAP-to-GAAP switch (application). None of these requires examining interrelationships or detecting discrepancies. The r3 TBS has no review or docreview part.
source: AICPA 2026 FAR Blueprint skill definitions (Application: calculate, prepare, determine; Analysis: analyze, reconcile, detect and correct)
fix: Relabel far-chg-10, -19, -21, -22, -24 and far-chg-chk1 as 'application'; far-chg-14 as 'remembering'; far-tbs-r3-changes-errors as 'application' (or add a review part, e.g. a prepared restatement schedule to check, to justify 'analysis').

issue: Difficulty is inflated: 16 of 31 practice and exam items are difficulty 3, including one-rule recall items and one-step computations. Identical computations carry different difficulties: far-chg-21 is 3 but far-chg-02 (the same net-of-tax cumulative effect) is 2; far-chg-24 is 3 but far-x3-13 (the same useful-life revision) is 2.
evidence: Difficulty 3 on: far-chg-14 and -28 (recall 'earliest date practicable'), far-chg-16 and -27 (cash basis → error), far-chg-26 (classification given in the stem), far-chg-21 (20,000 × 0.75), far-chg-24 (36,000 ÷ 3). Distribution in cues.md: {1: 6, 2: 9, 3: 16}.
source: Schema difficulty 1–3; internal consistency with far-chg-02 and far-x3-13
fix: Set far-chg-14, -16, -26, -27 and -28 to difficulty 1, and far-chg-21 and -24 to difficulty 2.

issue: Distractor (b) $7,200's explanation says 'That continues DDB at 40%', but continuing DDB gives $14,400, which is option (c). $7,200 is the $36,000 carrying amount spread over the original 5-year life instead of the 3 remaining years. A learner who picks (b) is told the wrong reason, and a false one.
source: ASC 250-10-45-19, 45-20 (prospective application of the new method to the carrying amount over the remaining life)
fix: (b) explanation: 'Divides the $36,000 carrying amount by the original 5-year life; only 3 years remain.' Trap: wrong-period (or wrong-rule). (a) explanation: 'Straight-line on original cost ignores the $64,000 already depreciated; use the $36,000 carrying amount.' Trap: wrong-rule.

issue: Several distractor trap labels and explanations don't describe the error that produces the option, or are circular. far-chg-22: (c) $14,545 and (d) $20,000 are labeled 'distractor-number' ('uses an irrelevant number from the facts'), and (d)'s explanation is just 'Not the computation.' In fact (c) = 100,000 × 8/55 (SYD fraction as if applied from inception, i.e., retrospective) and (d) = 80,000 × 2/8 (double-declining instead of SYD). (a) $10,000 ('keeps straight-line') is labeled wrong-classification. far-chg-24(c) $8,571 = 60,000 ÷ 7 (cost over the new total life) is labeled distractor-number. far-chg-25(d) $10,000 'Not the effect.' is circular (it doubles the error); (b) 'overstated by $5,000' ignores the 2025 reversal but is labeled wrong-rule, while the same error in far-chg-13(a) is labeled wrong-period. far-chg-21(b) (gross of tax) is labeled wrong-rule, while the identical error in far-chg-02, -03, -12 and -20 is labeled partial-computation; (c) (cumulative effect in current income) is labeled wrong-classification where far-chg-11 and -17 use outdated-rule. far-chg-17(d) 'only in the notes' is labeled partial-computation.
fix: far-chg-22: (a) trap wrong-rule; (c) explanation 'Applies the 10-year SYD fraction 8/55 to original cost, as if SYD had always been used; the change is prospective: book value × 8/36', trap wrong-rule; (d) explanation '80,000 × 2/8 is double-declining balance, not SYD', trap wrong-rule. far-chg-24(c): 'Divides cost by the new total life (4 + 3); use the $36,000 carrying amount', trap wrong-rule. far-chg-25(b) trap wrong-period; (d) explanation 'Doubles the error; the 2025 understatement offsets the 2024 overstatement', trap overgeneralization. far-chg-21(b) trap partial-computation; (c) trap outdated-rule. far-chg-17(d) trap wrong-rule.

issue: Both items set a 2024 error in comparative 2025/2024 statements, so the error arose in the earliest period presented. Their explanations say the after-tax effect adjusts 'opening retained earnings' (far-x3-29: 'adjust the opening balance of retained earnings for the earliest period presented'). For these facts, 1/1/2024 retained earnings is NOT adjusted: the 2024 income statement is restated, and only 12/31/2024 (opening 2025) RE changes. A learner applying the explanation literally would adjust 1/1/2024 RE and double-count. far-chg-23's key text 'RE down $7,500' and far-x3-29's key text 'adjust opening retained earnings' don't say which date.
evidence: far-chg-23: restated 2024 depreciation +10,000, 2024 NI −7,500, 12/31/2024 RE −7,500; 1/1/2024 RE unchanged. far-x3-29: restated 2024 NI +23,700; 12/31/2024 RE +23,700; 1/1/2024 RE unchanged. A cumulative adjustment to the earliest period's opening RE applies only to errors in periods before the earliest one presented.
source: ASC 250-10-45-23 (restatement: cumulative effect on periods before those presented goes to the opening balances of the first period presented; period-specific effects are reflected in each period presented)
fix: far-chg-23 key: 'Restate 2024 (depreciation +$10,000); 12/31/2024 retained earnings down $7,500'. Explanation: '2024 is presented, so its income statement is restated (NI −7,500). Retained earnings at 1/1/2024 is unaffected because the error arose in 2024.' far-x3-29: key 'Restate the 2024 statements (2024 net income increases by $23,700)'. Explanation: 'Because the error arose in 2024, the earliest period presented, 2024 is restated and 1/1/2024 RE is unchanged; an opening-RE adjustment would be needed only for errors in years before 2024.'

issue: Near-duplicate items in the same 28-item practice pool test the same fact the same way. far-chg-16 and -27 (cash basis → GAAP = error; also far-chg-chk1, fc5, TBS r3 c6 and TBS u12 r5: six times). far-chg-14 and -28 (impracticable → earliest date practicable; also far-chg-08). far-chg-13 and -25 (overstated ending inventory → RE correct after two years; also far-chg-06, far-iv-chk2 and far-iv-08 in far-inventory-valuation: five times). far-chg-pre1 and -15 (useful-life revision → prospective, 10→7 vs. 10→15 years). Meanwhile several testable points have no item at all (see the lesson findings): ASU transition provisions, the business-combination exclusion from reporting-entity changes, change-in-estimate disclosures, and the EPS effects of a restatement.
evidence: Stem Jaccard: far-chg-16/-27 0.61; far-chg-pre1/-15 0.45. far-chg-14/-28 have different wording but the same rule and an equivalent key ('From the earliest date practicable' / 'From the earliest period practicable'). far-chg-13/-25 are the same scenario with Year 1/Year 2 replaced by 2024/2025.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 7 (same fact tested the same way more than about 3 times)
fix: Replace far-chg-27 with an item on a change required by a new ASU (follows the ASU's transition provisions). Replace far-chg-28 with a partial-impracticability item (cumulative effect determinable at the start of the current year only → adjust that year's opening balances). Replace far-chg-25 with a counterbalancing error found while the second year's books are still open (requires a correcting entry). Keep far-chg-pre1 as the pre-question but change far-chg-15 to a combined life-and-salvage revision computation, or to a change-in-estimate disclosure item.

issue: Implausible distractors: (b) 'The name of the audit partner' and (d) 'Nothing, if the effect is favorable' can be ruled out without any knowledge of ASC 250, which leaves a 2-option item. This is not CPA-level realism.
evidence: Only (a) and (c) are plausible ASC 250 disclosures; (b) is unrelated to financial statement notes and (d) is an obvious absolute.
fix: Replace (b) and (d) with plausible wrong disclosures, e.g. 'Pro forma net income as if the new principle had been applied, shown only for the current year' (the pre-SFAS 154 APB 20 requirement, trap outdated-rule) and 'The effect on income from continuing operations only for the year of change, with no per-share amounts' (trap partial-computation; ASC 250-10-50-1(b) requires per-share effects for the current period and each prior period retrospectively adjusted).

issue: The calc flag is inconsistent across the three counterbalancing-inventory items. far-chg-13 is calc:true, but far-chg-25 (identical structure and options: none / over / under / doubled) and far-chg-06 are calc:false.
evidence: far-chg-13 calc True; far-chg-25 calc False; far-chg-06 calc False. All three are answered by the same two-year offset reasoning, with no arithmetic beyond recognizing +X − X = 0.
source: Schema: calc is set only for items that need a computation
fix: Set far-chg-13 calc to false (to match far-chg-25 and -06).

issue: Row explanations: c5 says 'Changing the entities in combined statements changes the reporting entity', but item 5 is presenting consolidated statements in place of separate statements, a different ASC 250-10-20 case. c3 says only 'A change in depreciation method is handled prospectively', without explaining why it is classified as a change in estimate effected by a change in principle rather than a plain change in estimate or principle, which is the exact distinction the dropdown tests.
evidence: Exhibit item 5: 'Presented consolidated statements for the first time in place of the separate statements of the parent and its long-held subsidiaries.' c5 explanation refers to 'combined statements'.
source: ASC 250-10-20 (Change in the reporting entity, cases a–c); ASC 250-10-45-18
fix: c5: 'Presenting consolidated statements in place of the individual entities' statements is a change in reporting entity (ASC 250-10-20), applied retrospectively.' c3: 'A depreciation-method change reflects a new estimate of the pattern of consumption of benefits, so ASC 250-10-45-18 treats it as a change in estimate effected by a change in principle: prospective, with preferability justified.'

issue: Journal part 'je' asks for 'the Year 3 entry to correct the machine error'. Many candidates (and review texts) include the current-year depreciation in the correcting entry, e.g. Dr Machinery 80,000; Dr Depreciation expense 16,000; Cr Accumulated depreciation 32,000; Cr Retained earnings 64,000. The scorer marks the combined credit (32,000) wrong and charges a cell for the extra Depreciation expense line, though the entry is valid. The prompt never says to exclude Year 3 depreciation; only the post-answer explanation does. The account list (which includes Depreciation expense) and maxLines 4 invite exactly that 4-line answer.
evidence: tbsScoring.ts scoreJournal: each expected line must match account, side and amount; unmatched entered lines cost a cell. Expected lines: Machinery Dr 80,000; Accumulated depreciation Cr 16,000; Retained earnings Cr 64,000. The 4-line combined answer scores 2 of 3 expected cells minus 1 extra-line penalty, about 1/3, for a correct entry.
fix: Amend the prompt: 'Record the Year 3 entry to correct the machine error only (record Year 3 depreciation separately; do not include it).' Alternatively, remove 'Depreciation expense' from the account list.

issue: Row r4 is based on 'Switching future depreciation of new buildings from straight-line to double-declining balance'. Applying a different method only to newly acquired assets has no effect on existing balances. Some candidates will wonder whether it is an accounting change at all (ASC 250-10-45-1 excludes principles adopted for transactions that are new or different in substance). The key (change in estimate effected by a change in principle — prospective) is the best of the options offered, but the wording adds avoidable doubt.
evidence: Exhibit 'Other changes under discussion', bullet 1, vs. dropdown label r4 'Straight-line → double-declining balance'.
fix: Reword the exhibit bullet to 'Switching depreciation of all buildings from straight-line to double-declining balance'.

issue: The faded example's credit-side tax entry ('Dr Deferred tax asset or Income taxes receivable 10,000') doesn't state its assumption. It is right only if the depreciation was also omitted from the tax return. In the more common case, tax depreciation was claimed and only the book entry was missed, and the correction reduces the deferred tax liability. Also, the flowchart has no branch for a change in reporting entity: following it for 'consolidated in place of individual statements' ends at 'Change in principle'.
evidence: Faded step 2 solution text. Flowchart: B (was the prior method GAAP?) → Yes → C (new estimate?) → No → F (depreciation method?) → No → G 'Change in principle'.
source: ASC 740-10 (deferred taxes on the book-tax basis difference); ASC 250-10-20
fix: Add to the scenario 'The depreciation was also omitted from the Year 2 tax return' (or change the entry to 'Dr Deferred tax liability 10,000' and state that tax depreciation was claimed). Add a flowchart node before C: 'Different set of entities presented?' → 'Change in reporting entity: retrospective'.

issue: Flashcard fc6's back is just 'Retrospective.' It doesn't say what counts as a reporting-entity change, or that a business combination doesn't. The six cards cover only the headline treatments; there are no cards for impracticability, indirect effects, counterbalancing errors, preferability disclosure or new-ASU transition, all of which the practice items test.
fix: fc6 back: 'Retrospective (recast all periods presented). Includes consolidated or combined statements in place of individual ones, or a change in the subsidiaries consolidated; NOT a business combination or VIE consolidation.' Add cards: 'Impracticable retrospective application' → earliest period practicable / prospective; 'Indirect effects (e.g., profit sharing)' → period of change; 'Counterbalancing error found after year 2 closes' → no entry, restate presented periods; 'Change required by a new ASU' → its transition provisions.
